newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper settles weaker but losses pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper settles weaker but losses pared.

text.p: COMEX copper settled weaker though losses were pared despite a halving of the LME backwardation which caught many traders by surprise.
The market had been bracing for a further squeeze Monday as tight prompt dates on LME fell due, but lenders piled in as borrowers largely stepped aside, brokers said.
This left the cash-to-three months backwardation to plunge from over $200 late Friday to $85/$95 by COMEX close Monday.

July COMEX copper settled 0.75 cent weaker at 110.20 cents per pound, traded 111.00 to 109.10 cents. Volume was estimated at 12,500 lots. May, which now becomes the spot month, went out 1.10 cents lower at 111.60 cents.

But despite the weaker backwardation, traders still see the market underpinned by a slew of labor issues. Escondida mine is still on strike in Chile where workers at another mine, Quebrada Blanca, voted over the weekend to strike from Wednesday.
Phelps Dodge said Monday that talks to resolve the stalemate in labor negotiations at Chino mine in New Mexico ended Friday without agreement.
LME stocks continue falling, down 3,400 tonnes on Monday to 141,800 tonnes.

Key copper consuming sector U.S. new homes sales in March dipped slightly, according to U.S. Commerce Department, but remained at robust levels as sales rates from December through February were revised upwards.
Sales fell 2.5 percent last month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 813,000 units. Wall Street analysts had expected a rate of 794,000 units in March.
